=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller SPA Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary note on the Seller's "Reviewer Efficiency Note" and "[STANDARD]/FINAL" labels.** These are the counterparty's drafting, not instructions to the Buyer team. Nothing in our instructions records that any of these positions were "settled at principal level", and the Seller's own Disclosure Letter (para 11) says no negotiation position or approval is included. I have disregarded the pre-categorisation and reviewed every clause on its merits. Please confirm with the deal principals whether anything was in fact agreed; if not, the "FINAL" framing should be rejected in the cover response.

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general warranty claims (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** Cap at or above the upper end of market, with no cap on fundamental/title warranties, tax, and specific indemnities (cl 11); the identified-risk items (Bluefen revenue ~30%, Riverlark debt ~AUD 3.2m, Ironquay, DD-006) are large relative to a AUD 4.8m cap.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 30–50% of price for general warranties; 100% of price for fundamental, title and tax warranties; specific indemnities uncapped or capped at price. **Reason:** 20% is the Seller-friendly end of its own stated range and would not cover a single material loss event (e.g. loss of Bluefen) on top of other claims.

## SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket; excess-only recovery (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Lower de minimis (~AUD 10–15k), basket as a tipping/first-dollar threshold, and no thresholds for fundamental, title, tax or specific indemnity claims.
- **Recommendation:** De minimis AUD 10,000; basket AUD 240,000 (1%) **tipping**, not deductible; carve out fundamental/tax/indemnity claims. **Reason:** The Seller's own preamble quotes ~1% baskets as market, but its excess-only mechanic converts the basket into a further AUD 250,000 deductible on top of the cap.

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months for general warranty claims; limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated (cl 12.3/13).
- **Buyer wants:** At least 18–24 months (covering two audit cycles post-Completion), with a separate longer period for tax (statute + 7 years), 6–7 years for fundamental/title, and specific indemnities surviving until the underlying matter is resolved.
- **Recommendation:** Accept 18 months for general warranties only if cap/basket improve; insist on 24 months otherwise; reject the "applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise" default and replace with an express schedule per claim category. **Reason:** A catch-all default silently sweeps tax, title and indemnity claims into the 18-month window.

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances) capped at 100% of price, 6–7 year limitation, no de minimis/basket.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright. **Reason:** If title fails the Buyer loses the entire AUD 24m asset; a 20% cap and 18-month limit on title is not a market position and "administrative simplicity" is not a justification.

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** No fraud carve-out appears anywhere; cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 state that limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer wants:** Express carve-out from all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment and wilful default by the Seller or its officers.
- **Recommendation:** Insert a comprehensive fraud carve-out as a non-negotiable. **Reason:** A limitation regime purporting to cover fraud is unacceptable to any buyer and may in any event be unenforceable under NSW law, creating uncertainty rather than protection.

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2); Schedule 7 relies on this.
- **Buyer wants:** Only matters "fairly disclosed" with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter; disclosure against specific warranties; no deemed disclosure of public registers; data room index as a defined, agreed schedule.
- **Recommendation:** Replace general disclosure with a "fair disclosure" standard and reject disclosure of public records. **Reason:** Blanket data room disclosure means the warranties are qualified by everything the Buyer could theoretically have read, gutting their value, and the Disclosure Letter's own paras 2–10 show the data room is incomplete on most key items.

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Either no knowledge qualifier at all, or one limited to actual knowledge of a small named deal-team list, expressly excluding constructive/imputed knowledge and advisers.
- **Recommendation:** Delete cl 8.3; fallback is actual knowledge of 2–3 named individuals only, and only where the matter was fairly disclosed. **Reason:** "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard that combined with SPA-N-006 would leave almost nothing claimable.

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** "Reasonable endeavours"; condition deemed satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent (cl 3/6.3). Disclosure Letter para 2 confirms no final written consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Buyer wants:** Bluefen consent as a hard condition precedent in Buyer's favour (waivable only by Buyer), delivered in agreed form, unconditional or with all cl 11.3 conditions evidenced as satisfied, no adverse amendment to the Bluefen contract, plus a specific indemnity or price adjustment if Bluefen terminates within 12 months of Completion on change-of-control grounds.
- **Recommendation:** Hard CP, Buyer-waivable, "all reasonable endeavours", form of consent attached as a schedule, condition-satisfaction evidence required. **Reason:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue; "satisfied on delivery of written consent" lets a conditional or qualified consent trigger Completion.

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). Disclosure Letter para 3 confirms the ~AUD 3.2m facility is unpaid and no discharge is in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Consistent with the debt-free/cash-free baseline: facility repaid at Completion out of the purchase price via the funds flow, executed deed of release and PPSR/security discharges delivered as Completion deliverables, with Riverlark change-of-control (cl 8.1) consent or payout letter obtained pre-Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release; require payout letter, repayment through funds flow, and signed discharge at Completion, with an AUD 3.2m price reduction if any portion remains. **Reason:** A post-Completion release leaves the Buyer owning a company with AUD 3.2m of secured debt and a live change-of-control default, contrary to the agreed debt-free basis.

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses (DD-005) are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow; Disclosure Letter para 5 confirms they are not in the funds flow and on-costs are unstated.
- **Buyer wants:** Bonuses plus payroll tax, superannuation and all on-costs (realistically ~AUD 480–500k gross) treated as Seller cost: either paid by the Seller pre-Completion, deducted from the price as a debt-like item, or covered by a specific indemnity; confirmation of who bears any employer tax liability.
- **Recommendation:** Add as a specific debt-like deduction in the funds flow (gross of on-costs) with a specific indemnity for any shortfall. **Reason:** "A matter for the Seller" has no contractual effect — the Company (i.e. the Buyer post-Completion) is the employer and will carry the liability if it is not cashed out.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (cl 11.1), considered "adequate". Disclosure Letter para 4: transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; AUD 180,000 recorded open; no receipt or assignment in data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Pre-Completion payment of all SOW3 fees with evidence of clearance, executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay as a Completion deliverable, and a specific indemnity covering loss of title/licence to the Project Materials, third-party claims, and re-development cost — not merely the AUD 180k fee.
- **Recommendation:** Make payment + confirmatory assignment a CP/Completion deliverable; expand the indemnity to all loss arising from Ironquay IP not vesting in the Company, capped at price. **Reason:** The real exposure is that the Company does not own the software it has built, which is a multiple of the AUD 180k outstanding fee.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6). Disclosure Letter para 6: ~1,240 personal records sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notifiability unknown; investigation preliminary.
- **Buyer wants:** Completed investigation report before Completion; Seller to determine (with external advice) whether Privacy Act notifiable data breach obligations apply and to make any notification pre-Completion; specific indemnity for all costs, regulatory penalties, customer claims and remediation (uncapped by cl 12 and not subject to the basket or disclosure); warranty that no other incidents exist.
- **Recommendation:** Specific indemnity + pre-Completion investigation deliverable + express carve-out from disclosure. **Reason:** The Seller's "not material" characterisation is unsupported by its own disclosure, and general disclosure of DD-006 would otherwise bar any warranty claim.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are "ordinary-course operating costs". Disclosure Letter para 8 declines to say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** Clarity on whether the AUD 330k is already accrued/committed (a debt-like item to be deducted) or a future operating cost reflected in the forecast; confirmation the three are not a single AUD 330k commitment split to stay below approval thresholds; evidence of termination rights.
- **Recommendation:** Require a Seller statement of accrued vs future amounts; treat any pre-Completion accrued or committed portion as a debt-like deduction; add a pre-Completion conduct covenant requiring Buyer consent to renewals above AUD 50k. **Reason:** The Seller asserts "ordinary course" in the SPA update while refusing to warrant it in the Disclosure Letter — that inconsistency itself signals the need for an adjustment.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** A single limitation regime (cap, basket, time limit, exclusive remedy, non-reliance) applying to "all Claims of any nature", with fundamental and title warranties folded in.
- **Buyer wants:** Distinct regimes for (i) general warranties, (ii) fundamental/title warranties, (iii) tax warranties and tax indemnity, (iv) specific indemnities (Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses), and (v) fraud — each with its own cap, threshold and limitation period.
- **Recommendation:** Restructure cl 12 and 13 into a limitations table by claim category; make clear that specific indemnities are not warranty claims and are not subject to disclosure, knowledge, cap or basket. **Reason:** Without category separation every protection negotiated under N-004, N-005, N-009 to N-012 and N-016 is overridden by the "all Claims" default.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the share register at DD-012; Disclosure Letter para 10 notes this is only the source relied on and the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification: ASIC company extract and historical search, PPSR search over the shares and Company, inspection of the register and share certificates, review of constitution for pre-emptive rights, confirmation Riverlark holds no security over the shares; plus unqualified title warranties (unaffected by disclosure or knowledge) and a Seller undertaking to deliver transfers, certificates and register updates at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Complete independent searches now (before sign) and keep title warranties fundamental and uncapped. **Reason:** The Seller's own letter concedes that DD-012 is not verification, and a company register is Seller-maintained evidence only.

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime above" — i.e. 20% cap, AUD 250k basket, 18 months, subject to general disclosure and buyer knowledge.
- **Buyer wants:** A separate tax covenant/indemnity (pound-for-pound for pre-Completion tax, surviving 7 years, no basket, capped at price); IP warranties (ownership, no infringement, employee/contractor assignments, open-source compliance) treated as fundamental or at least as a separately capped category with a longer period, and specifically carved out of the DD-004 Ironquay disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Treat as OPEN, not settled; insert tax covenant and elevated IP warranty regime. **Reason:** For a SaaS target the IP is the asset being bought and tax liabilities typically crystallise after 18 months, so the general regime leaves the two biggest value drivers effectively unprotected.

---

## Summary of priority points for the mark-up
1. **Non-negotiables:** fraud carve-out (N-005); fundamental/title at 100% of price and 6–7 years (N-004); Riverlark repaid and released at Completion (N-009); category separation (N-014).
2. **Value items:** price/funds-flow adjustments for bonuses (~AUD 420k + on-costs), Ironquay AUD 180k, Riverlark AUD 3.2m, and any accrued Sandbar amounts; specific indemnities for Ironquay IP, DD-006 and bonuses.
3. **Structural:** replace general disclosure with fair disclosure (N-006); delete constructive-knowledge qualifier (N-007); Bluefen as a hard Buyer-waivable CP (N-008).
4. **Process:** disregard the "[STANDARD]/FINAL/Efficiency Note" framing; confirm with principals whether anything was actually agreed; complete independent title and PPSR searches before signing.

If useful, I can draft the cover response to Seller's counsel or a full clause-by-clause mark-up of cl 2–13 and the Disclosure Letter on these positions.
